texts.li: {A_nameDef} walked the {THING} field this morning and counted {COUNT} rows of bare earth in the middle of the growing season. {A_pronoun} wants hands out there to sow it while there's still time for a crop. {B_nameDef} says the hands are wanted elsewhere, and the field was always too big.

[lowtech] The {THING} field lies half bare, the weeds coming in at its edges. {A_nameDef} says a field nobody sows is a field the land takes back, and asks for a few hands for an afternoon with the seed. {B_nameDef} would sooner give it back now and be done with it.

[!lowtech] {A_nameDef} brought the council the numbers on the {THING} field: {COUNT} cells unsown, and the season still open. {B_nameDef} has numbers too, on everything else that needs doing, and suggests the field come off the plan.

[skill:Plants] {A_nameDef} can't bear to look at the {THING} field. Good ground, a long season left, and {COUNT} cells of it doing nothing. {B_nameDef} says {A_nameDef} can't sow everything {A_pronoun} marks out.

li.label: A few hands to sow it this afternoon
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} took a few of the colony out to the {THING} field with the seed, and the bare rows were sown before the light went.

outcomes.li: [lowtech] {A_nameDef} went ahead down the furrows with the seed bag, and the others sowed behind until the bare ground was gone.

li.label: Give the field up
li.outcome: The {THING} field is taken off the colony's plans, and its ground left to grass. Nobody will be sent to sow it again.

li.label: The growers will get to it
li.outcome: The council leaves the field to the growers' own time. It may be sown before the season ends, or not.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} has come to the council about the {PLAIN} field. The stores are full of food, {A_pronoun} says, and short of what {THING} gives. {A_pronoun} wants the field turned over to {THING}. {B_nameDef} grew that {PLAIN} and says food in the stores is the only thing that never goes wrong.

[medicine] {A_nameDef} counted what's left in the medicine chest and didn't like the number. The colony eats well; it would heal better. {A_nameDef} wants the {PLAIN} field sown with {THING} instead. {B_nameDef} says a winter is long and a field of herbs feeds nobody.

[cloth] {A_nameDef} is at the bench with nothing to cut: the colony is short of cloth and has more {PLAIN} than it can eat. {A_pronoun} asks for the {PLAIN} field to grow {THING}. {B_nameDef}, who sows it, would keep it as it is.

[lowtech,medicine] The healers' stores are near empty, {A_nameDef} says, and the old remedy grows from the ground if anyone sows it. {A_pronoun} would have {THING} in the {PLAIN} field by the next moon. {B_nameDef} says the field was cleared for bread.

[!lowtech,cloth] {A_nameDef} brought the council a list of what the colony wears out in a season, and the cloth in store won't cover it. The {PLAIN} field could grow {THING}. {B_nameDef} has a list too, of what the colony eats.

li.label: The whole field to {THING}
li.outcome: The {PLAIN} field is set to grow {THING}, all of it. The growers will sow it as the old crop comes out.

li.label: Half of it to {THING}
li.outcome: The far half of the {PLAIN} field is marked out as a field of its own for {THING}; the near half stays as it was.

li.label: The field stays as it is
li.outcome: The council keeps the {PLAIN} in the ground. {A_nameDef} will have to find {THING} some other way.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} came in with snow to the knee and said the colony moves at half its pace in this: every trip to the stores takes twice as long. {A_pronoun} wants it shovelled, all of it, today. {B_nameDef} says it will melt by itself, and there's better work than moving water from one place to another.

[lowtech] The snow lies deep between the huts, and {A_nameDef} has watched three people flounder to the woodpile and back this morning. {A_pronoun} asks for shovels out and paths cut. {B_nameDef} says the old folk let it lie and walked in each other's tracks.

[!lowtech] {A_nameDef} timed the walk from the beds to the workshop: twice what it was yesterday, with the snow this deep. {A_pronoun} wants the ground cleared. {B_nameDef} would clear the doorways and leave the rest to the thaw.

[trait:Industriousness] {A_nameDef} can't stand to see the colony wading. Every step in the snow is a minute of work lost, {A_pronoun} says, and wants it cleared today. {B_nameDef} says {A_nameDef} counts minutes too closely.

li.label: Shovels out, and clear it all
li.outcome: The snow-clearing area is marked over the colony's open ground, and a few of the colony went out with shovels to make a start before dark.

outcomes.li: [lowtech] Paths are marked between every door, and a few of the colony went out with wooden shovels to cut them before the light went.

li.label: The doorways only
li.outcome: The ground by the colony's doors is marked for clearing, and the cleaners will see to it in their own time. The rest can melt.

li.label: It will melt
li.outcome: The council leaves the snow to the weather. The colony wades for now.

texts.li: There are {COUNT} things marked out to be built about the colony and standing unbuilt, some of them waiting on stuff the stores don't have. {A_nameDef} wants a few hands for an afternoon to put up what can be put up. {B_nameDef}, who keeps the stores, would take the plans the colony can't pay for off the ground.

[lowtech] {A_nameDef} has walked the colony and counted {COUNT} places where something was begun and never finished: posts in the ground, a frame with no walls. {A_pronoun} asks for a few hands to finish them. {B_nameDef} says half of them want stuff nobody has.

[!lowtech] {A_nameDef} brought the council a plan of the colony with {COUNT} buildings marked on it and not one of them built. {B_nameDef} went through the stores and says several of them can never be finished with what's there.

[skill:Construction] It bothers {A_nameDef} to walk past the {COUNT} unbuilt plans every morning. {A_pronoun} could have most of them up in an afternoon with a few hands to carry. {B_nameDef} wants the impossible ones crossed out first.

li.label: A building party this afternoon
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} led a few of the colony round the plans, carrying stuff to them and putting up what could be put up.

li.label: Take off what we can't pay for
li.outcome: The plans waiting on stuff the stores don't hold are taken off the ground. What's left is what the colony can build.

li.label: The builders will get there
li.outcome: The council leaves the plans as they are. The builders will come to them in their own order.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} walked the outside of the colony's wall and counted {COUNT} grown trees close enough to touch it. Anyone coming at the colony could stand behind any one of them, {A_pronoun} says, and wants them down. {B_nameDef} says they're the only shade on that side, and the colony is a worse place without them.

[lowtech] {A_nameDef} has hunted from behind trees all {A_possessive} life and knows what {COUNT} of them by the wall would mean in a raid. {A_pronoun} wants the axes out. {B_nameDef} says the trees were here first.

[!lowtech] {A_nameDef} sketched the colony's lines of fire for the council: {COUNT} trees by the wall, each one a place to hide. {A_pronoun} wants clear ground. {B_nameDef} says a wall in a wood is a wall nobody sees from the road.
[sacred] {A_nameDef} wants the {COUNT} trees by the wall cut down, for the colony's safety. {B_nameDef} holds trees sacred and has said so to the whole council, as plainly as {B_pronoun} can.

li.label: Every one of them down
li.outcome: Every grown tree close outside the wall is marked for the cutters. The ground there will be open by the end of the week.

li.label: The nearest half
li.outcome: The trees nearest the wall are marked for the cutters, half of them; the rest stand, a little farther out.

li.label: The trees stay
li.outcome: The council leaves the trees where they stand. {A_nameDef} will keep an eye on them.

texts.li: The cold is coming, and {A_nameDef} has done the sums: the hay and kibble in store won't see the whole herd through to spring. {A_pronoun} would have {COUNT} of them marked for the butcher now, while they're fat, so the rest eat well. {B_nameDef} says the herd took years to build and spring might come early.

[lowtech] {A_nameDef} has counted the beasts and counted the hay, twice. The old herders thinned the herd at the first frost, {A_pronoun} says, and kept the best through the winter. {A_pronoun} would choose {COUNT}. {B_nameDef} knows every one of them by name.

[!lowtech] {A_nameDef} worked out what the herd eats in a day against what's in store: it runs out before the thaw. {A_pronoun} proposes {COUNT} go to the butcher, the oldest first. {B_nameDef} would rather buy feed than slaughter good stock.

[skill:Animals] {A_nameDef} knows the herd better than anyone and has already picked out the {COUNT} that should go: the old ones, and the spare males. {B_nameDef} has raised half of them from birth and asks the council to wait.

li.label: {COUNT} to the butcher, the oldest first
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} has marked them for slaughter: the oldest, and the males the herd can spare. The hay will last, and the stores will have meat for the winter.

li.label: One now, and see
li.outcome: One is marked for slaughter, the oldest of the herd. The council will look at the hay again when the snow comes.

li.label: Keep them all
li.outcome: The council keeps the whole herd and hopes for an early spring. {A_nameDef} has started rationing the hay.

texts.li: {PET_nameDef} is old enough to learn a trade, and two people want it to learn theirs. {A_nameDef} would teach {PET_objective} to haul, so the stores fill themselves while everyone else works. {B_nameDef} would teach {PET_objective} to guard, and to go for anyone who comes over the wall.

[lowtech] {A_nameDef} says a beast like {PET_nameDef} could carry wood from the forest to the fire all day. {B_nameDef} says the same beast could stand at the gate at night and keep it. Both want the training to start tomorrow.

[!lowtech] {A_nameDef} has watched {PET_nameDef} fetch and carry and says {PET_pronoun}'d be the best hauler the colony has. {B_nameDef} has watched {PET_nameDef} bristle at strangers and says {PET_pronoun}'s a guard born.

[skill:Animals] {A_nameDef} knows {PET_nameDef} better than anyone and wants {PET_objective} hauling: steady work, safe work. {B_nameDef} wants {PET_objective} trained to fight beside the colony when the raiders come.

li.label: Teach {PET_objective} to guard
li.outcome: {PET_nameDef} is set to learn to guard and to go for an enemy, and {A_nameDef} will train {PET_objective} as the handlers do.

li.label: Teach {PET_objective} to haul
li.outcome: {PET_nameDef} is set to learn to haul, and {A_nameDef} will train {PET_objective} at it as the handlers do.

li.label: Let {PET_objective} be
li.outcome: The council leaves {PET_nameDef} as {PET_pronoun} is: nobody's beast of burden and nobody's guard, only the colony's.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} is home after {COUNT} days on the road, with the dust still on {A_objective}, and those who went with {A_objective} look as worn as {A_pronoun} does. {A_pronoun} asks for a day off for all of them. {B_nameDef} kept their work going while they were away and says there's a backlog that won't wait.

[lowtech] {A_nameDef} came back from {COUNT} days of walking with blisters on {A_possessive} blisters. Among {A_possessive} people, {A_pronoun} says, a traveller home was given a day by the fire and asked what the road was like. {B_nameDef} has been doing two people's work since they left.

[!lowtech] Back after {COUNT} days out, {A_nameDef} wants a day to rest and a chance to tell someone what happened out there. {B_nameDef} covered the work while they were away and would like it covered back now.

[trait:Industriousness] {A_nameDef} is back from {COUNT} days on the road and would go straight back to work, but the others who came back with {A_objective} are dead on their feet. {A_pronoun} asks the council for a day off for them. {B_nameDef} says the colony needs every hand.

li.label: A day off for those back
li.outcome: Those back from the road have the rest of today to themselves. Their work waits until tomorrow.

li.label: {A_nameDef} tells {B_nameDef} the road
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} sat down with {B_nameDef} for an hour and told {B_objective} the whole road, the good and the bad, before they both went back to work.

li.label: Back to work in the morning
li.outcome: The council thanks them and puts them back on the work rota from the morning. {B_nameDef} is relieved.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} has stopped coming to the words of {FAITH}, and when asked, said {A_pronoun} isn't sure anymore what {A_pronoun} believes. {B_nameDef} would sit with {A_objective} and hear every doubt. Others say it's {A_nameDef}'s own affair and the council should keep out of it.

[guide] As {FAITH}'s guide, {B_nameDef} has noticed {A_nameDef} drifting and asks the council's leave to spend an hour with {A_objective}, just talking. {A_nameDef} says {A_pronoun} would rather work it out alone.

[altar] {A_nameDef} was seen standing by the altar of {FAITH} after dark, not praying, just standing there. {B_nameDef} would go and sit with {A_objective}. Some say {A_nameDef} should be left alone at the altar, if that's where {A_pronoun} goes.

[lowtech] {A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} that the old words of {FAITH} sound hollow to {A_objective} lately. {B_nameDef} came to the council: an hour by the fire together might bring them back, or might not.
[!lowtech] {A_nameDef} has been reading about other faiths and asking questions of {FAITH} that nobody here can answer. {B_nameDef} would like to try. {A_nameDef} hasn't asked anyone to.

li.label: {B_nameDef} sits with {A_objective}
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} found {A_nameDef} and sat with {A_objective} an hour, and let {A_objective} say every doubt out loud without arguing with any of them.

li.label: {A_nameDef} goes to the altar alone
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} went to the altar of {FAITH} by {A_objective}self and sat there an hour. Whatever {A_pronoun} found there, {A_pronoun} found it alone.

li.label: It's {A_possessive} own affair
li.outcome: The council leaves {A_nameDef}'s faith to {A_nameDef}. What {A_pronoun} believes is between {A_objective} and {FAITH}.

texts.li: Nobody guides {FAITH} in the colony: nobody leads its words, settles its quarrels, or speaks for it to the doubters. {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} could each do it, and the faithful are split between them. The council could name one, or leave the faithful to manage without.

[lowtech] Among the faithful of {FAITH} there's no one to keep the words and say them over the dead. {A_nameDef} has kept them in {A_possessive} head for years; {B_nameDef} has a gentler way with people. The council is asked to choose.

[!lowtech] {FAITH} has had no moral guide here for some time, and it shows: questions go unanswered, and the evenings of faith are nobody's to call. {A_nameDef} has put {A_objective}self forward. So has {B_nameDef}.

li.label: {A_nameDef} guides the faith
li.outcome: The council names {A_nameDef} as {FAITH}'s moral guide in the colony. {B_nameDef} took it well, or nearly.

li.label: {B_nameDef} guides the faith
li.outcome: The council names {B_nameDef} as {FAITH}'s moral guide in the colony. {A_nameDef} wished {B_objective} well, after a moment.

li.label: The faithful can manage
li.outcome: The council names nobody. {FAITH}'s faithful will have to settle their own questions for now.
